pllc.structure_note: A PLLC is a type of LLC (Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Title 3, Chapter 101 applies generally) with an additional professional-licensing layer on top (Title 7, Chapters 301 and 304). Most categories below mirror llc.json directly since the base LLC governance/financial/operational mechanics are the same entity. The professional_licensing_compliance category is what's genuinely new and exclusive to PLLCs -- it exists because Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Section 301.007 restricts PLLC ownership and management to individuals actually licensed in the profession the PLLC renders (or qualifying 'professional organizations' of similarly-licensed people), which has no equivalent in a plain LLC.

identity: Certificate of Formation (Professional Limited Liability Company)
Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Status
governance: Buy-Sell Agreement (Ownership Transfer Restricted to Licensed Professionals)
statutory: Texas Business Organizations Code Chapters 301 and 304 Compliance
Texas Business Organizations Code Chapter 101 Compliance (base LLC provisions)
Texas Franchise Tax Public Information Report (PIR) Filing
Foreign Qualification Filings (if operating in other states)
professional_licensing_compliance: Individual Professional License Verification (Managers, if manager-managed)
Professional Organization Ownership Documentation (if an owner is itself a qualifying professional organization rather than an individual)
Entity Name Compliance Certification (PLLC designator and governing-profession ethics-rule check)

State Licensing Board Registration (the specific board depends on the profession -- e.g. TSBPA for a CPA-owned PLLC, Texas Medical Board for a physician-owned PLLC, State Bar of Texas for an attorney-owned PLLC)

Certificate of Formation (Professional L: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Title 1, Chapter 3, Subchapter A (general formation provisions) and Title 7, Chapter 304 (PLLC-specific formation rules) -- filed via Secretary of State Form 206, a distinct form from the plain-LLC Form 205. CONFIRMED 2026-08-30 directly against the Texas Secretary of State's own Form 206 instructions.
Company Agreement (Operating Agreement): Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Section 101.001(1) and Section 101.052 -- the base LLC company-agreement provisions apply to a PLLC the same way they apply to a plain LLC, since a PLLC is a type of LLC under Title 3.
Texas Business Organizations Code Chapte: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Title 7: Chapter 301 establishes ownership/management restrictions -- only a licensed professional individual or a qualifying 'professional organization' may be an owner or manager, and only a professional individual may be an officer (Section 301.007). Chapter 304 sets the PLLC-specific formation and operation rules. CONFIRMED 2026-08-30 directly against the Texas Secretary of State's own Form 206 instructions.
Individual Professional License Verifica: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Section 301.007 -- an individual may be a governing person, member, or officer of a PLLC only if licensed (in Texas or another jurisdiction) to provide the same professional service the PLLC renders. This is the core compliance fact this category exists to track; it has no equivalent in the plain-LLC entity file.
Entity Name Compliance Certification (PL: Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code Section 5.059 (entity name must contain the phrase 'professional limited liability company' or an abbreviation such as 'PLLC') and Section 5.060 (the name also cannot conflict with any law or ethics rule governing the profession rendered through the PLLC).
Registered Agent Designation: Standard Texas registered-agent requirement, same as a plain LLC -- but the Texas Secretary of State's own Form 206 instructions specifically flag an elevated consequence for a PLLC: failure to maintain a registered agent and registered office may result in involuntary termination of the professional entity.
